correctness.rationale: The simplex sum and positivity follow from the exact homogeneous replicator vector field. With s=u1+u3-u2-u4, x=u1-u3, y=u2-u4, C=(1-s^2)/4 and d(log(product_i u_i))/dt=a s^2 exactly. For a>0 the product lower bound confines every interior trajectory to a compact positive simplex set; LaSalle reduces omega limits to s=0; there s-dot=-(a+2)xy and (x,y) is a nonzero rotation unless x=y=0, hence the maximal invariant subset is U. For -1<a<0 a positive product limit would imply interior precompactness and force convergence to U, contradicting strictly submaximal initial product and monotone decrease, so product->0 and min_i u_i->0. For a>0, eigenvalues -a/4, ±i(a+2)/4; the quadratic center-manifold invariant polynomial h_2=4(a+2)^2(x^2-y^2)/D - 4a(a+2)xy/D (D=a^2+4(a+2)^2) has zero invariance residual. The quartic radial drift angular average is -a(a+2)^2/(2D), positive damping; periodic normal-form transform yields dot Z=-beta Z^2+O(Z^(5/2)), hence tE->1/beta. The unique strong stable manifold is the invariant x=y=0 line; all other interior orbits exponentially track the center manifold. SymPy independently checked the exact h_2 identity and angular mean; two integrations to T=6000 exhibited finite-time approach, not proof of the asymptotic claim.
